notes: D1 oracle is docs/nagoya-d1/oracle-clash-report.md's 'Station roster (D1 transcription)' section, hand-transcribed by Nico from Wikipedia's aggregate station list and six per-line articles. Not generated from GTFS - no official Nagoya Metro GTFS/GTFS-RT/route-map PDF exists (see hazard-pack.md H0, the top hazard in this pack).
City id nagoya. Display Nagoya. Agency Nagoya City Transportation Bureau (名古屋市交通局). Not Osaka, not Tokyo, not a Keihanshin/Japan super-city. Do not invent city=nagoya-metro, nagoya-subway, ngy.

City stays planned. Modes v1: Nagoya Municipal Subway only - six lines (Higashiyama, Meijo, Meiko, Tsurumai, Sakura-dori, Kamiiida). Meitetsu (all lines, incl. Seto Line at Sakaemachi, Komaki Line beyond Kamiiida, Inuyama Line beyond Kami Otai, Toyota/Mikawa Line beyond Akaike), JR (Tokaido, Chuo, Shinkansen), Aonami Line, Nagoya Municipal Bus are out.

No official public GTFS or GTFS-RT of any kind (harder starting position than Osaka, which at least has an official EN/JP station-list page and a dated route-map PDF). Transitland 0 hits. Mobility Database 0 rows for Nagoya Metro. Nagoya is not an ODPT member as of 2 Sep 2026 (Tokyo Metro is - not a safe generalisation for all Japan subways). No env key. adapterReady false. See hazard-pack.md H0.

Locked hub: Sakae / 栄 (H10 x M05 only, per the oracle report's explicit rider-site transfer statement). Underground-connected but NOT folded in: Hisaya-odori (M06 x S05, separate physical station) and Sakaemachi (Meitetsu Seto Line, different operator, out of v1).

Meijo (M) is a TRUE LOOP - no linear terminus, closes on itself at Kanayama (M01). Direction model is clockwise/anticlockwise, same topology as Copenhagen M3 Cityringen. See direction-model-memo.md section 3.

Meiko (E) is a BRANCH off the Meijo loop at Kanayama, with real through-running trains crossing the M/E boundary ('roughly every other anticlockwise Meijo loop train diverts here'). This pack flags but does not model that through-running board behaviour. See hazard-pack.md H4 and direction-model-memo.md section 4.

Through-run OUT: Meitetsu Seto Line at Sakaemachi (near Sakae, different operator); Meitetsu Komaki Line beyond Kamiiida K01; Meitetsu Inuyama Line beyond Kami Otai T01; Meitetsu Toyota Line / Meitetsu Mikawa Line beyond Akaike T20. JR Tokaido/Chuo at Nagoya and Kanayama stations. Aonami Line (separate operator, automated people mover).

INTERNAL SOURCE CONFLICTS flagged, not silently resolved (hazard-pack.md H1a): Kamiiida Line terminus codes (roster gives K01=Kamiiida/K02=Heian-dori; earlier oracle-report prose called Kamiiida 'K02'); Meiko branch origin code (roster gives E01=Kanayama; earlier oracle-report table gave 'E00'); Aratama-bashi's codes (roster gives M23/S14, doubly self-consistent across both lines' own tables; earlier oracle-report table gave 'M07/S06'). This pack uses the roster table's values throughout, none confirmed against the (nonexistent) official feed.

UNIQUE STATION COUNT DISCREPANCY (hazard-pack.md H1b): the oracle report's own summary claims 87 unique stations. Mechanically unioning the six roster tables as transcribed (96 raw line-ticks, merging one same-place spelling variant - Aratama-bashi/Aratamabashi) yields 83. uniqueStationCount below reflects the 83 actually present in these arrays. Not forced to match 87 - flagged for Nico to reconcile against the official Nagoya City Transportation Bureau count.

Direction: line + official terminus for the five linear/branch lines (e.g. H + Fujigaoka, E + Nagoyako). Meijo (loop) is clockwise/anticlockwise, never a fake terminus pair. See direction-model-memo.md.
No stopIds in this file. No GTFS route ids (none exist). Passenger line tokens are the official roman letters H / M / E / T / S / K plus the official EN/JP line names.
coverageGaps: No official public GTFS / GTFS-RT / route-map PDF of any kind exists for Nagoya Metro (top hazard, hazard-pack.md H0). Do not generate this file from a feed that does not exist.

Station graph is one hop further from a primary source than the Osaka precedent - hand-transcribed from Wikipedia's aggregate list and six per-line articles because the oracle report found no dedicated official map PDF on the rider site as of 2026-09-06.

Meitetsu Seto Line at Sakaemachi (near Sakae). Meitetsu Komaki Line beyond Kamiiida K01. Meitetsu Inuyama Line beyond Kami Otai T01. Meitetsu Toyota Line / Meitetsu Mikawa Line beyond Akaike T20. All out of v1.
JR Tokaido / Chuo / Shinkansen at Nagoya and Kanayama stations. Aonami Line. Nagoya Municipal Bus. All out of v1.
Meijo/Meiko through-running board behaviour (some physical trains cross the M/E boundary at Kanayama) is flagged, not modelled. See direction-model-memo.md section 4.

Kamiiida Line K01/K02 numbering and Meiko branch E00/E01 numbering both have an unresolved internal conflict between the oracle report's own prose and its Station roster table. Roster values used here; not confirmed against a live source. See hazard-pack.md H1a.
Aratama-bashi's M/S codes also have this internal conflict (roster: M23/S14; earlier oracle-report table: M07/S06). Roster value used here. See hazard-pack.md H1a.
Unique station count: oracle report claims 87; this pack's mechanical union of the roster tables yields 83. Not reconciled - see hazard-pack.md H1b.
No official EN wording confirmed for Meijo's clockwise/anticlockwise chip (direction-model-memo.md open question 1) - no official rider-site page was found to check this against.

Hub lock (M05 x H10). Underground to Hisaya-odori M06 (separate station).
M06 x S05. Underground complex with Sakae; doNotGroup vs Sakae (separate physical station).

M03 x T09 Tsurumai.

lines.note: Opened 1965. TRUE LOOP - no linear terminus. 28 stations. Roster: 'M01 Kanayama (start/end point) -> M02-M27 -> M28 Nishi Takakura (final station before loop closes back to M01)... Loop runs anticlockwise (when viewed on standard map orientation).' Same topology as Copenhagen M3 Cityringen (docs/copenhagen-d1/direction-model-memo.md section 1) - direction model is clockwise/anticlockwise, not line+terminus; see direction-model-memo.md section 3. Do not invent a fake linear terminus pair. Meiko (E) branches off this loop at Kanayama with real through-running trains - see meiko line note and direction-model-memo.md section 4.

lines.name: Meiko

branches.note: Junction with Meijo M01 - same physical station. Roster uses E01 for this branch origin; an earlier oracle-report table used E00 for the same place (hazard-pack.md H1a) - E01 used here as the roster's own tabulated value.

lines.note: Opened 1971. Branch off the Meijo loop at Kanayama, serving the port district. 7 stations. Roster: 'Roughly every other anticlockwise Meijo loop train diverts here rather than continuing to Nagoya Daigaku; integrated service.' This is a genuine through-running hazard, not a cosmetic branch note - see hazard-pack.md H4 and direction-model-memo.md section 4. This pack does not model the through-running board behaviour, only flags it.

lines.name: Kamiiida

lines.note: Opened 2003. Only 2 stations, 0.8 km - shortest subway line in Japan by station count. Meitetsu Komaki Line through-run beyond Kamiiida (K01) continues to Komaki and Inuyama - out of v1; v1 stops at K01.
